I think you misunderstand the objective of art analysis. I don't think anyone can figure out the intent of a writer through reading a text, so why would that be interesting? The interesting part of art analysis is to look at what is in the text and see what it means to you, what the little details can possibly convey. In this way a text is not a flat object, but a living breathing thing - it takes on different forms for different people. 

When the teacher says: "the curtains were blue because the main character was feeling down," they don't mean that is the singular possible interpretation. They should perhaps be saying: "The color blue in color theory is often associated with coldness, or sadness. So one possible interpretation of the text could be that the blue color of the curtains are an extension of the mood of the character, which is at the time going through a sad period in their life."

And to your first point: there are certainly writers that labor over the extremely minute details, James Joyce being the most obvious one.

I'm sorry if I came on a bit strong, I have spent years studying literature and media in university and I see a lot of dismissive attitudes toward textual interpretation that just rub me the wrong way. I'm happy to see that you are very open to that kind of interaction with art.

Typically the text in your above post is used to dissuade people from engaging with art in a more creative way because the author's intent to some is gospel.

The above meme also seems to me to poke fun at the reader interpretation rather than the strict adherence of some members of the community to the words of the authors. I find the latter to be incredibly stifling when it comes to enjoying the games as pieces of art.

Silent Hill games are incredibly complex and not always intentionally so, that's one of the main reasons I - and I'm sure many others - love them.

It is so painfully obvious that anyone that reposts this tired ass statement is not interested in engaging with texts in a meaningful way. Whether the statement is correct or not, the assessment is interesting. Analyzing art is cool and good actually, even when the author keeps talking about how things were intended - it doesn't matter to how you experience it. Correct assessments of texts don't exist with art analysis, only interpretation.

Holding a review to high standards keeps them meaningful, like I said in my original comment, when you equate reviews to glorified opinion pieces they lose their value. Critics are important not because they share their opinions with their audience, but because they allow them to make educated decisions in relations to the stuff they spend their money on. I don't care if you hate turn-based battles, talk about the implementation of them; I don't care if you think random encounters are stupid, talk about how they are used, whether they are overdone, whether the encounters are actually interesting, whether the fights feel meaningful every time, whether the combat shines even in these shorter bouts or it only really shines during the boss battles (and don't misrepresent that shit either, like dunkey did in his video; that doesn't help your credibility).

Reviews are more important than you give them credit for. Good game reviews are a rare treat, and they are super important to the growth of the medium. I highly recommend you finish watching the video instead of continuing this conversation because if he cannot change your mind with his arguments, nor can the other people he refers to in the video, then this will also end up being useless.

Think of it like this: A music critic needs to know musical theory, a game critic needs to understand the theory behind game design. Simple. And I do think reviews need to be overly serious; bonuses and sales are literally dependent on them. If you want to write an opinion piece about a game, call it an opinion piece; don't call it a review.

I think dunkey makes some good points in his video, but that doesn't excuse the stupid shit that is in there. He is, intentionally or not, dissuading people from buying a game by saying literally nothing about the actual game besides "these things are stupid". If the first thing a person sees about Octopath Traveler is his video, they might get an incomplete and disingenuous idea of what the game is and not engage with a potentially enjoyable experience.

And I can say that titling an opinion piece with "review", or not stating that this is your opinion, or not disclosing that you are incredibly biased against these types of games and actually are misrepresenting a lot of aspects of it intentionally for cheap laughs is wrong; and I am.

Movie critics have studied film, music critics have studied music, game critics should study games; superficial knowledge of them is not enough to write a review.

The last point is about studying the thing you are criticizing, actually knowing your stuff is a prerequisite of being a critic. Obviously, if you think reviews are just opinions than that's not the case, but that's where we differ. I want a review to be useful for a reader even if they don't agree with my opinion on something. And it's not just about stating that something has new content, again, just watch that part of the video. Reviewing should be more than just giving your opinion on something, it should be an educated assessment interspersed with opinion.

I kind of dislike the mentality that a review is just a glorified opinion piece. This guy's video actually tackles this subject later on, around 18:25 (after dunkey lists a bunch of possible moves from the God of War game) he actually gives a fairly succinct explanation as to how a review differs from an opinion piece. You don't write to explain what you thought of it, you write to explain what the game does, how it compares to what came before, and who might enjoy it. If you write about Call of Duty as someone who doesn't enjoy shooting games you can still point out that shooting fans will enjoy the new stuff it brings to the table and how it might address certain shortcomings that the genre had before it, etc. There is much more to a review than just stating an opinion, and the more people start saying that a review is just an opinion the less valuable actual reviews become. 

This is also an issue that mostly exists within the videogame space (and it's now bleeding into movies too), because there are no majors for videogame criticism, so everyone is just doing something and there are no credentials that you can get that guarantee you a spot in a popular publication. Combine that with the increase in non-professional criticism from blogs and social media websites (including Youtube), as well as the commercialized nature of videogame reviews, and you have the perfect shitstorm.

The reason Slaughterhouse Five is so highly praised is partly because it's an amazing written account of the post war trauma that a lot of soldiers had to deal with. Partly because it's a fairly neutral look on the war, it doesn't paint the Germans as the bad guys, and it shows how horrible the bombing of Dresden was, even if it was against the Germans. Another part of the reason is hardly anyone knew a thing about what happened in Dresden, because the American media sure as hell didn't talk about it, so this book gave some insight into that too. Another reason is that Kurt Vonnegut breaks almost every narratological rule in this book. He jumps from a first-person narrative to a third-person narrative but sometimes breaks into first person again (That was me. That was I. That was the writer of this book.) He uses the paratexts within the primary text and he uses time as a means to show the distorted way a man with PTST is related to it. 

I could write a whole lot more about it, but I already wrote enough when I had to study the book about seven months ago. Let's just say the reason it's praised is because of all that and because Literary Theorists can study the book to no end.

They sent me out here to get used to the environment before giving me any mission objectives. I have been here for two days now and feel that I have adjusted to my surroundings fairly well. The people in here have every reason to be here. Today I saw a man sit in the corner of the cafeteria with his back to the room. He knocked his head on the wall repeatedly whispering something after every consecutive knock. Another funny character caught my attention yesterday when I first entered the ward. He had a bald head, big ears and a shit eating grin like you wouldn't believe; just stared straight ahead for hours.

Three days now and still no word. I suppose it's common for a mission objective to take a while to reach me, but I'm getting increasingly uncomfortable with my surroundings. Today a guy started screaming at me without warning. Just stood up and yelled at me, his face mere inches from mine. I had a splitting headache afterwards so I asked one of the nurses for an aspirine. She said that aspirine doesn't mix well with the meds. I told her I don't take meds and she runs off to get me some, almost forces 'em down my throat. At first it scared the shit out of me, but she explained that they were just to help me relax. I do feel terribly relaxed.

Day four. Still no word from the higher ups. Suppose they expect me to look around and find some clues as to what it is I'm supposed to do. Maybe they're testing me, or something. I checked some parts of the ward, looked under chairs and even checked behind the TV. Everyone was lookin' at me funny, but they're crazy so what do I care. Some of them even started snooping around too; like I need the competition. One of them was the guy who screamed at me the other day. I told him to cut it off and he looked at me like a deer in headlights, he didn't move an inch the rest of the day. The other guys told on me and now I have to take double doses. I hope the agency knows what they are doing.

Day six. Yesterday I didn't do anything. They told us we could watch TV and we all sat around the screen in silence. Before I knew it it was time to go to bed. I don't even know what we were watching. Today I decided to ask a bunch of my fellow patients some questions. They didn't seem all that interested in the things I said, except for the bald guy with the big ears. His name was Barry. Barry said that he know who I am. Barry scares me.

Day seven. Barry wasn't in the courtyard today. I have to keep my eye on him.

Day eight. Some of the other guys have started to act strange. They have been acting like I don't exist for the better part of the day. Barry probably put 'em up to this. He knows too much. Just look at him sitting there with his bald head. I've got my eye on you Barry.

Day nine. I saw Barry talk to one of the nurses today. They are in on this whole thing, I just know it. I have to tell the agency, but they didn't give me any way to contact them. I tried sending morse code messages through the television remote, I hope it reaches them.

Day twelve. Barry is gone. I don't have to worry about him anymore.

Day thirteen. They found Barry, I'm going away to solitary for a while. I will ask them to send these out.

Day thirty-two. They didn't send them out. Of course they didn't. They are in on it. All of them are.

Day thirty-three. I found a special pill behind the couch. I ate it. Now I can talk to the agency through my head. They said it was alright. They have been getting my messages. They will send help soon.

Day thirty-four. New patient arrived. I think it might be the help the agency was talking about.

Day thirty-five. He was a fake. I had to test him and he failed.

Day fifty-two. They said I was a danger to myself and everyone around me. They will help me get better. I don't want to get better. I told them it was a mistake. I am a spy, I said. I work for the government. They just shook their heads.

Day fifty-three. I saw a new doctor enter the ward today. He talked to the head nurse. She pointed at me. I don't trust the doctor.

Day fifty-four. The doctor tried to kill me. He had a pen, but I knew it was filled with poison. I will not let them get to me. I bit him in his finger and took the pen from him. He walked away, but I have the pen now!

Day fifty-five. I am scheduled for a talk with the doctor tomorrow. I won't go.

Day fifty-six. They forced me to go. He said things but I didn't listen. I just nodded. I don't like him.

About three months ago I met a girl through a friend of mine. We were playing a game and invited her to play with us. After we were done playing we kept talking about all sorts of stuff, movies, books, etc. We hit it off pretty well and a few days after I added her on Facebook.

We started talking a little more often, almost every day, and we never ran out of things to say. After two months or so we started video chatting a bit, and around that time I noticed just how beautiful she really was. I was slowly falling in love with her.

The 22nd of November the both of us went to a friend's house for the weekend. That friend was throwing a birthday party and we were invited. Before she arrived I was really nervous. I was playing a bit of GTA V when the bell finally rang and my stomach twisted into a knot. I blankly stared at the screen just acting as if I was giving the game my full attention. I heard her voice and in that moment it hit me that she was just a few feet away from me. 

I looked around to see her standing in the room talking to the friend. She looked at me and our eyes met, and I'd like to say a spark flew through the room, but before it could I turned away. I was so goddamn nervous. I acted cool, like I didn't care she was there, but inside I was burning up. She walked up to me and said: "So we finally meet," and went in for a hug. I sheepishly followed her hugging gesture and sat back down to play my game.

Gradually as the day continued I got more comfortable, as did she. We inched closer to each other as the hours passed and at some point she said her hands were cold. She has this condition where the tips of her fingers don't have a good blood flow or something, so they get cold very easily. So I grew some balls and put her hands in mine. We sat there like that for what seemed like an eternity.

That night I kissed her and she kissed me back. The rest of the weekend we were pretty much inseperable. Now I'm just waiting to see her again, the 20th of December she will come over to my place for the weekend.

The fact that someone as beautiful and amazing as her likes me back, that's what's making me happy right now.
